search.website_text: Dalamud MCP is a Dalamud plugin for FINAL FANTASY XIV. It provides a local Model Context Protocol server for AI-assisted plugin development, runtime inspection and in-game validation. # DalamudMCP English | [简体中文](README.zh-CN.md) DalamudMCP is a [Dalamud](https://github.com/goatcorp/Dalamud) plugin for FINAL FANTASY XIV. It provides a local [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) server for AI-assisted plugin development, runtime inspection and in-game validation. The plugin runs within the game process and exposes character, object, party, inventory, game-data and UI state through Dalamud services and [FFXIVClientStructs](https://github.com/aers/FFXIVClientStructs). It also provides validated raw-memory reads, event collection, screenshots and inter-plugin communication. The current catalog contains **123 tools: 74 read-only and 49 mutating**. Mutating tools require explicit enablement. The default endpoint is `http://127.0.0.1:18777/mcp`. HTTP-capable MCP clients connect directly; stdio-only clients use the included bridge. > **Validation scope:** Offline checks cover protocol, schemas, loading and selected native-memory operations. > Live coverage is limited to the scenarios documented in the [tool audit](docs/tool-audit-2026-10-17.md) > and [screenshot guide](docs/screenshots.md). These results do not establish compatibility with every client or game state. ## Contents - [Install from a plugin repository](#install-from-a-plugin-repository) - [Build](#build) - [Install as a dev plugin](#install-as-a-dev-plugin) - [Configure](#configure) - [Connect an agent](#connect-an-agent) - [Tool reference](#tool-reference) - [Safety model](#safety-model) - [Architecture](#architecture) - [Verification](#verification) - [Limitations](#limitations) ## Install from a plugin repository Published releases are available from [NiGuangOwO's Dalamud plugin repository](https://github.com/NiGuangOwO/DalamudPlugins). Repository index: ```text https://raw.githubusercontent.com/NiGuangOwO/DalamudPlugins/main/pluginmaster.json ``` 1. Launch the game with Dalamud enabled. Enter `/xlsettings` in chat to open Dalamud settings. 2. Under `Experimental`, locate `Custom Plugin Repositories`. Add the index URL above and save the settings. 3. Enter `/xlplugins` to open the Plugin Installer. Refresh the list and install **DalamudMCP** by **NiGuangOwO**. Subsequent releases are available through the same installer. 4. Enter `/dalamudmcp status` to inspect listener status, or `/dalamudmcp` to open plugin settings. After installation, follow [Configure](#configure) and [Connect an agent](#connect-an-agent) to complete client setup. Mutating tools remain disabled until enabled in plugin settings. New releases may take several minutes to appear because of GitHub's index cache. When replacing a development installation, disable the dev copy before enabling the repository version. ## Build The project uses [`Dalamud.NET.Sdk`](https://www.nuget.org/packages/Dalamud.NET.Sdk). Build the plugin project directly from the repository root: ```powershell dotnet build src\DalamudMCP\DalamudMCP.csproj -p:Platform=x64 ``` Dalamud assemblies are resolved from the local launcher installation. `src\DalamudMCP\Directory.Build.props` selects the CN installation when present and preserves an existing `DALAMUD_HOME` override. Otherwise, the SDK uses its default launcher location: - `%APPDATA%\XIVLauncherCN\addon\Hooks\dev` - `%APPDATA%\XIVLauncher\addon\Hooks\dev` For a custom installation, set `DALAMUD_HOME` or specify the assembly directory: ```powershell dotnet build src\DalamudMCP\DalamudMCP.csproj -p:Platform=x64 -p:DalamudLibPath="D:\some\Hooks\dev\" ``` The repository contains separate project files for the plugin, bridge and tests; it does not contain a solution file. The SDK supplies the Dalamud, Lumina, Newtonsoft.Json and FFXIVClientStructs references, together with DalamudPackager. Using FFXIVClientStructs from the installed Dalamud distribution maintains consistency with that distribution's structure definitions. ### Packaging DalamudPackager generates the manifest from `src\DalamudMCP\DalamudMCP.csproj` during the build. Output paths below are relative to `src\DalamudMCP`: | Configuration | Output | | --- | --- | | `Debug` (default) | `bin\x64\Debug\DalamudMCP.dll`, `DalamudMCP.json` and `DalamudMCP.deps.json` | | `Release` | Release binaries and `bin\x64\Release\DalamudMCP\latest.zip` for repository distribution | ```powershell dotnet build src\DalamudMCP\DalamudMCP.csproj -p:Platform=x64 -c Release ``` `latest.zip` contains `DalamudMCP.dll`, `DalamudMCP.json` and `DalamudMCP.deps.json`. The icon is also copied to `images\icon.png` beside the package and embedded in the plugin assembly. The [build workflow](.github/workflows/build.yml) produces Release artifacts on pushes and pull requests. Published packages are distributed through the plugin repository listed above. ## Install as a dev plugin For local development, register the Debug assembly directly: ```text \src\DalamudMCP\bin\x64\Debug\DalamudMCP.dll ``` Keep the generated `DalamudMCP.json` and `DalamudMCP.deps.json` beside the DLL. To test a Release package, extract `latest.zip` to a separate directory and register the extracted DLL. ### Activating in-game 1. Open `/xlsettings`. Under `Experimental`, add the full DLL path to `Dev Plugin Locations`. 2. Open `/xlplugins`, select `Dev Tools > Installed Dev Plugins`, and enable `DalamudMCP`. 3. Run `/dalamudmcp status` to verify listener status. `Enabled` and `AutoStart` default to `true`. The development-plugin location is retained in Dalamud settings. Loading and automatic-start options are managed through the Plugin Installer. ## Configure Open **DalamudMCP** settings with `/dalamudmcp` or the Plugin Installer's configuration button. | Setting | Default | Description | | --- | --- | --- | | `Enabled` | `true` | Enables the listener. | | `AutoStart with the plugin` | `true` | Starts the listener when the plugin loads. | | `Port` | `18777` | TCP port, limited to 1024–65535 and bound to `127.0.0.1`. | | `Framework timeout (s)` | `10.0` | Framework-thread execution timeout, limited to 0.5–120 seconds. | | `Allow mutating tools` | `false` | Makes tools that can change game or plugin state available to clients. | | `Auth token` | empty | Shared authentication token; an empty value disables authentication. | | `Max object results` | `200` | Per-query object limit, constrained to 1–5000. | | `Max memory read (bytes)` | `65536` | Maximum raw-memory read size, constrained to 16–1048576 bytes. | | `Log every MCP request` | `false` | Records method, request ID, tool name, outcome and duration. Changes apply immediately. | | `Language` | `auto` | UI and command-feedback language. Supports automatic selection, English and Simplified Chinese. Changes apply immediately. | Port and framework-timeout changes require a listener restart using `Restart listener`. Other settings apply immediately. Edits are saved when the edited control loses focus; `Save now` provides an explicit save action. The window also provides listener controls and `Open config folder`. With `Language: auto`, the UI follows the game client's language. Translation tables are embedded in the DLL; unresolved translation keys fall back to English. `AllowMutatingTools` is enforced for both discovery and invocation. When disabled, mutating tools are omitted from `tools/list` and rejected by `tools/call`. ## Connect an agent Connection setup and skill installation are separate operations. The [agent setup guide](docs/agent-setup.md) covers MCP registration, skill discovery and installation in other plugin projects. The included [Dalamud development skill](.agents/skills/dalamud-development/SKILL.md), repository [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md) and server initialization instructions describe the development workflow. Skill selection depends on the agent's discovery mechanism. The [addon and development-loader guide](docs/addon-probes-and-dev-loader.md) describes frame-aligned UI sampling, conditional input, node lookup and development-plugin loading. Use the connected tool schemas as the parameter reference. `tools/list` is paginated; continue with `nextCursor` until all pages have been retrieved. All endpoints bind to `127.0.0.1`: | Endpoint | Method | Purpose | | --- | --- | --- | | `/mcp` | POST / GET / DELETE | Primary Streamable HTTP transport. | | `/sse` | GET | Legacy HTTP+SSE transport for protocol revision `2024-11-05`. | | `/messages?sessionId=...` | POST | Legacy message endpoint paired with `/sse`. | | `/health` | GET | Listener status, tool count, protocol versions, session count and access settings. | | `/tools` | GET | Tool catalog with names, descriptions and mutation classifications. | | `/` | GET | Server information and transport endpoints. | Supported protocol revisions are `2025-06-18`, `2025-03-26` and `2024-11-05`. After `initialize`, requests must include the `Mcp-Session-Id` response header received during the handshake. A missing session returns HTTP `400` with `session_required`; an expired or unknown session returns HTTP `404` with `session_not_found`. The client must initialize a new session after either response. When an authentication token is configured, requests require: ```text Authorization: Bearer ``` Authentication applies to `/health` and `/tools` as well as MCP traffic. `OPTIONS` and `GET /` are exempt. The server also accepts `?token=` for clients that cannot set headers. The following example illustrates an HTTP-capable MCP configuration. Configuration keys depend on the client implementation: ```json { "mcpServers": { "ffxiv": { "type": "http", "url": "http://127.0.0.1:18777/mcp", "headers": { "Authorization": "Bearer " } } } } ``` Omit `headers` when authentication is disabled. ### stdio-only clients `bridge\DalamudMcpBridge` provides a console bridge for clients that launch a subprocess and exchange newline-delimited JSON-RPC over stdin/stdout. Set the client's `command` to the bridge executable. The plugin DLL runs inside Dalamud and is not a stdio executable. ```powershell dotnet build bridge\DalamudMcpBridge\DalamudMcpBridge.csproj -c Release ``` ```json { "mcpServers": { "dalamud": { "command": "C:\\path\\to\\DalamudMCP\\bridge\\DalamudMcpBridge\\bin\\Release\\net10.0\\dalamud-mcp-bridge.exe" } } } ``` The bridge accepts `--port`, `--url`, `--token` and `--verbose`. It also reads `DALAMUD_MCP_PORT`, `DALAMUD_MCP_URL` and `DALAMUD_MCP_TOKEN`. The default server address is `http://127.0.0.1:18777`. The bridge retains the HTTP session header, reinitializes invalid sessions and retries the original request once. Before processing stdin, it checks `/health`; authentication failures terminate startup with a diagnostic message. Protocol output is written to stdout and diagnostics to stderr. Check server availability before configuring the client: ```powershell Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:18777/health Invoke-RestMethod http://127.0.0.1:18777/tools | ConvertTo-Json -Depth 4 ``` ## Tool reference The catalog contains 123 tools: 74 read-only and 49 mutating. The tables summarize the principal tools and parameters. The server's `tools/list` schemas define the complete catalog and argument constraints.
